newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr flinches as data remind of rate risk.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr flinches as data remind of rate risk.

text.p: The Australian dollar drifted toward the floor of its recent range at midday as local and U.S. banks probed for rumoured exporter bids under US$0.7490.
Dealers said sentiment had been soured by another failure at US$0.7520 overnight and by a sharp selloff against the Canadian dollar following a surprise rate hike from the Bank of Canada.

Canada joining the tightening club along with the U.S. and U.K., left Australia looking exposed as one of the few economies in the world on an easing bent. There had been some cooling in rate cut talk here, but a soft set of vehicle registrations data for May this morning reminded everyone where the risks lay.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the local dollar had drifted to US$0.7486/91 from an early US$0.7495/00 and US$0.7509/14 late here Thursday.

Key support at US$0.7470 had cushioned the currency for almost two weeks now and dealers expected it to hold until the monetary policy outlook -- hopefully -- became clearer after the Reserve Bank's monthly board meeting on July 1.

Some in the forex market this week had been playing down the chances of another cut in official rates after this meeting but the median of analysts' expectations surveyed by Reuters still had it as a 50 percent chance.

The easing camp would have been reassured by the motor vehicle registrations data which showed a 0.7 percent fall in May when analysts had looked for a bounce of around 1.5 percent in a natural correction to April's hefty 6.1 percent drop.
The fall saw trend registrations turn lower for the first time since September last year and reinforced the impression the consumer had turned very cautious in the second quarter.
It also boded ill for the May retail trade data due next Wednesday where analysts were in the similar position of forecasting a bounce in sales following a shock 1.7 percent dive in April.

It was also significant for the A$ since it and the Canadian dollar tend to be seen as interchangeable by offshore investors. Both are part of the informal dollar bloc, both are commodity linked currencies and the economies are similar in many ways.
With domestic policy still in an easing phase, the interest differential between the two currencies was set to narrow sharply and put the A$ under pressure in the short term.

Key support is seen around C$1.0205, which marked a trough in February this year, a break of which would return the A$ to territory not visited since January 1996 and threaten a slide to parity and beyond.
The A$ had tumbled to C$1.0334/44 by the midsession from C$1.0484/95 ahead of the Canadian hike.

However, analysts felt the prospect of further Canadian tightening would derpress the bond market there and could encourage portfolio switching out of Canadian bonds and into the better performing Australian bond market.
This in turn would tend to support the A$ over time.
Elsewhere, the dollar was off at 84.99/09 yen from 85.45/55 late Thursday and at 56.8 in trade weighted terms from 57.0.
